**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed)

The assignment framework across §10.2(a), §5.3, §7.6 and §7.1 meets the preferred position on every material term:

- **Our assignment rights (Depositor):** §10.2(a)'s restriction is expressly subject to §5.3, which delivers the full affiliate/successor carve-out — merger, consolidation, succession to the business, or assignment to an Affiliate all pass automatically with no counterparty consent, subject only to post-closing assumption, opinion and notice mechanics.
- **Symmetry:** The restriction binds the Depositor and the Servicer (Cellco) identically, with §7.6 as the Servicer's mirror carve-out.
- **No change-of-control exit:** Nothing in the document gives Cellco a termination, resignation or re-pricing right on our change of control. §7.1 affirmatively bars the Servicer from resigning unless legally unable to perform, and §7.4 constrains who may succeed it (≥$50,000,000 net worth, acceptable to the Owner Trustee and Indenture Trustee).

Two minor sub-elements sit short of the ideal preferred wording and are noted in the rationale only, not flagged: the residual consent standard lacks a "not unreasonably withheld" qualifier, and there is no express competitor bar. Neither is material — the residual consent runs to the trustees, Certificateholders and 66-2/3% of the Controlling Class, i.e. structural noteholder protection rather than counterparty leverage against us, and §7.4 already gates successor identity.
